names.name: Beignet
names.said: Square, no hole, and the sugar is not optional.

text.what: A deep-fried pastry of French origin, in New Orleans a square of dough fried until it puffs hollow and buried in confectioner's sugar. Beignet means bump.
text.story:
The pâte à choux method — butter, eggs, milk or water, sugar, flour, salt, cooked and beaten — is the style French immigrants brought to New Orleans in the 1700s. Beignets are also made from yeast-leavened batters and from rice flour, and the word covers all of them. In Canadian French, beigne or beignet simply means doughnut. In the former French colonies of West Africa a beignet is a ball of fried dough, sometimes millet flour in Senegal.

The New Orleans beignet arrives at a table three to an order with a snowbank of powdered sugar and coffee cut with chicory beside it.
text.how: Roll the dough thin, cut squares, fry hot so they inflate and stay hollow, then sugar them heavily while they steam.
text.today: A donut shop in Louisiana may sell beignets, donuts and king cake off the same counter without anyone treating that as a mixed menu.

kin.as: The stand that made the square one famous.
The other American donut lifted by steam alone.
